title: Unified treatment of local dynamical interactions in correlated metals using Eliashberg theory
authors: Jan Berges, Samuel Poncé, Mario Caserta, Nicola Marzari, Tommaso Chiarotti
abstract: First-principles studies of materials with strong electronic correlations introduce additional theoretical complexities and computational costs, even more so if lattice degrees of freedom also play a role. To address these challenges, we show how direct and phonon-mediated electron-electron interactions can be treated consistently. The key observation is that the GW and Fan-Migdal self-energies are topologically the same diagram, so that they can be unified using a single effective interaction, which is the sum of the two interactions. The Dyson equation for the electron Green function then yields normal-state Eliashberg equations, which can be viewed as a subset of the Hedin-Baym equations for coupled electrons and phonons [Phys. Rev. X 13, 031026 (2023)]. We solve these dynamical equations in a local approximation to calculate from first principles the temperature-dependent quasiparticle spectrum, with close attention to the low-energy window determining transport. We apply this extended dynamical Hubbard approach to the correlated metal Sr$_2$RuO$_4$, which has long served as a benchmark system for advanced electronic-structure methods. The resulting renormalization of quasiparticle bands is in qualitative agreement with experiments and results from dynamical mean-field theory. However, here the low-energy linewidth and associated resistivity within the Green-Kubo formalism in the bubble approximation are underestimated, suggesting the need for vertex corrections. This work highlights how simple dynamical formulations can provide an extensible framework for studying correlated materials, which treats electronic and vibrational excitations on equal footing.
summary: This work develops a unified theoretical framework to consistently treat both direct Coulomb and phonon-mediated interactions in correlated metals. By unifying the GW and Fan-Migdal self-energies, the authors derive and solve extended Eliashberg equations for the quasiparticle spectrum. The method is applied to $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$, demonstrating its utility while also pointing toward necessary vertex corrections for quantitative accuracy.
main_problem: To provide a unified theoretical framework for treating both direct electron-electron and phonon-mediated dynamical interactions in correlated metals.
main_result: The method successfully calculates the temperature-dependent quasiparticle spectrum for $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$, showing qualitative agreement with experiments, though vertex corrections are suggested for accurate resistivity.
method: The approach unifies GW and Fan-Migdal self-energies into a single effective interaction, leading to normal-state Eliashberg equations solved via a local approximation.
model_or_system: The study focuses on correlated metals, using $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$ as a benchmark system. The theory treats coupled electrons and phonons dynamically.
key_observables: Temperature-dependent quasiparticle spectrum, electrical resistivity (via Green-Kubo formalism), and spectral function $A(\epsilon)$.
important_parameters: Low-energy window, temperature ($T$), and the coupling strengths between electronic and vibrational excitations.
main_assumptions: The calculation is performed in a local approximation, and the need for vertex corrections is highlighted as a key limitation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the crystal structure, reciprocal space, and electron/phonon dispersion relations for $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the unified self-energy formalism, derives the resulting Eliashberg equations, solves these dynamical equations for the quasiparticle spectrum, and applies the framework to calculate transport properties for $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state correlations, the rigorous treatment of coupled electronic and vibrational dynamics using advanced Green's function techniques provides a powerful, generalizable framework for open quantum systems where environment coupling (phonons) is crucial.

figures.caption: Figure 1. (a) Crystal structure and (b) reciprocal space of Sr2RuO4. The primitive translation vectors, Brillouin-zone boundaries, and special k points of the simple (body-centered) tetragonal lattice are shown in gray (black). Note that the labels for the M and X points are often swapped in the case of the simple tetragonal lattice (see Fig. 4 of Ref. 55). (c) Electron and (d) phonon dispersion from DFT and DFPT along the path drawn with dashed lines in (b). The low-energy bands dominated by the d orbitals of the Ru atoms are shown as thick lines; the t2g bands have been Wannier interpolated. Orbital characters and longitudinal (L), transverse (T), and out-of-plane (Z) phonon displacements...

Figure 2. Spectral functions of (a) the effective interaction and (b) the bare and screened Green functions of the Ru-t2g manifold of Sr2RuO4 at T = 300 K. (c, d) Energy dependence of retarded electron self-energy at T = 300 K with and without the phonon-mediated part of the interaction. The inset is a close-up of the low-energy behavior of the imaginary part. (e, f) Temperature dependence of the renormalization factor and broadening at the Fermi level. The DMFT results, excluding phonon-mediated interaction, are from Hunter et al. [76].

Figure 3. Renormalized electronic structure of Sr2RuO4 at T = 5 K compared to results from DFT and ARPES [37]. (a) Spectral function. (b) Fermi surface for kz = 0. The β and γ sheets only cross in the absence of SOC.

Figure 4. Transport properties of Sr2RuO4. (a) In-plane resistivity from the direct, phonon-mediated, and effective electron–electron scattering as a function of temperature. Theoretical reference data is from Abramovitch et al. [26], experimental data from Tyler et al. [81]. (b) Normalized in-plane optical conductivity from the effective interaction at T = 290 K. Experimental data is from Stricker et al. [82].

Figure 5. Different ways of calculating the retarded electron self-energy of Sr2RuO4 at T = 300 K. (a, b) Comparison of one-shot local G0f W0 and self-consistent local G f W0 calculations on the real axis, enforcing ReΣiα(0) = ReΣiβ(0) for all orbitals α,β. (c, d) Comparison of G0f W0 calculations directly on the real axis using Eqs. (10) and (11) and on the imaginary axis using Eq. (16) with subsequent analytic continuation via Padé approximants.
